This is an application seeking bail in FIR No. 10/2022 dated 12.11.2022, under Sections 13(1) (c)
(a) and 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act read with Sections 409/420/120-B IPC, registered at Police Station- ACB/New Delhi.

2. The FIR has been registered by Delhi Jal Board (hereinafter referred to as DJB ) which had awarded the work of setting up of automative bill payment collection machines at different locations in different DJB offices for facilitating consumers to make bill payments.
The contract was given to Corporation Bank and was extended from time to time.
The Corporation Bank entered into a contract with M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions who in turn further sub contracted the work to Aurrum E-Payment Pvt. Ltd.
The applicant herein was the Director of Aurrum E-Payment Pvt. Ltd.
It is stated in the FIR that DJB funds to the tune of more than Rs. 20 crores have been embezzled.

3. Ms John, learned senior counsel appears on behalf of the applicant who was the Director in Aurrum E-Payment Pvt. Ltd and states that the Erstwhile Corporation Bank (now Union Bank) has filed an application before the DRT for recovery of 5.75 crores against M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions Rajenderan Nair vs State Nct Of Delhi on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195433928/
1 only.

sentences.text: She states that a bare perusal of the status report would show that in the present case over the years, the applicant has deposited about 466 crores collected from the kiosk.
She states that had there been any intention of cheating, such huge amount would not have been deposited by Aurrum.
She further states that at best it is recovery proceedings and filing of FIR cannot be used for recovery of monies.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
5. The respondent No.1 has filed a status report.
The newly impleaded respondent No.2-Delhi Jal Board is supporting the stand of respondent No.1.
6. Since the Delhi Jal Board is supporting the stand of the respondent No.1 there is no need for Delhi Jal Board to file a reply.

7. The Corporation Bank has filed recovery proceedings against M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions for Rs.
5.75 crores only and not against Aurrum or applicant .
The fact whether the amounts are due and payable by Aurrum or M/s Fresh Pay IT Solutions can only be adjudicated at the stage of trial.
The applicant has in the past transferred 466 crores amounts recovered for and on behalf of Corporation Bank.
As regards the dishonest intention, if any, on the part of the applicant can only be inferred after the parties have led evidence and not at the stage of bail.
Prima facie, the fact that Rs. 466 crores collected from the kiosk have been deposited further fortifies the absence of dishonest intention on the part of the applicant.

8. Learned counsel for the applicant states that in order to show applicant s bonafides, a sum of Rs.
50 lakhs shall be deposited with Registrar Delhi High Court within three days of his release and another sum of Rs. 1.5 crores will be deposited within 8 weeks of his release.
9.

sentences.text: 10. The amounts deposited by the applicant shall be without prejudice to his rights and contentions to be finally adjudicated at the appropriate stage.
11. This order is also passed only for the purposes of adjudicating the bail application and is without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties.
12. The petitioner has also placed on record the application filed by Corporation Bank before DRT.
Status report is taken on record.
13. The application is disposed of accordingly.
As prayed, copy of this order be given dasti under the signatures of the Court Master.
JASMEET SINGH, J APRIL 21, 2023 sr
